_about: Curated fishery notes for major waters. Species lists are general and compiled from state agency lake/river profiles; verify current regs, limits and advisories with ADCNR (outdooralabama.com) and GA DNR WRD (georgiawildlife.com). 'center' is an approximate label point; null means 'shown only when tapping the NHD water feature'. Edit freely — the pipeline joins these onto NHD by gnis_names.

waters.name: West Point Lake
waters.manager: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Mobile District
waters.notes: Big timbered creek arms; crappie around brush and bridges in spring. Hybrids school on main-lake points summer/fall. Boundary water — AL/GA reciprocal license applies on the main reservoir (check current terms).

links.label: Georgia DNR West Point fishing forecast & map

waters.name: Lake Harding (Bartletts Ferry)
waters.notes: Heavily developed shoreline with docks — skip docks and seawalls for spotted bass. Halawakee and Mountain Oak creek arms on the Alabama side. Fall drawdown most years.

waters.name: Goat Rock Lake
waters.notes: Narrow, riverine lake below Bartletts Ferry Dam; current from generation positions fish on points and eddies — check the generation schedule.

waters.name: Lake Oliver
waters.notes: Upper end below Goat Rock Dam fishes best when they are generating.

waters.name: Chattahoochee River (Columbus–Phenix City fall line)
waters.notes: Urban whitewater course below North Highlands Dam. Water rises fast and dangerously during releases — always check the generation schedule and USGS gauge before wading or paddling.

waters.name: Lake Eufaula (Walter F. George Lake)
waters.manager: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Mobile District
waters.notes: Ledges and grass for bass; crappie on brush piles and standing timber in creek mouths. Eufaula NWR on the upper lake.

waters.name: Lake Martin
waters.notes: Deep, clear, rocky lake. Alabama (spotted) bass dominate; stripers on the lower lake in winter. Winter drawdown most years — watch for exposed hazards.

waters.name: Yates Lake
waters.notes: Small riverine lake below Martin Dam; current-driven bite during generation.

waters.name: Thurlow Lake
waters.notes: Tiny lake above Tallassee; limited access.

waters.name: R.L. Harris Lake (Lake Wedowee)
waters.notes: Clear, rocky, steep banks; Tallapoosa and Little Tallapoosa arms.

waters.name: Tallapoosa River (free-flowing reaches)
waters.notes: Great float-fishing water between Harris and Martin (Horseshoe Bend area) and below Thurlow. Releases from Harris Dam change flows quickly.

waters.name: Lake Ogletree
waters.notes: Municipal water-supply lake — city permit and boating rules apply. Verify current rules with the city before fishing.

waters.name: Chewacla Lake
waters.notes: Small park lake; check park rules for boats and motors.

waters.name: Lee County Lake
waters.location_note: Approximate map reference from the official lake location link.
waters.notes: 321 Lee Road 808, Opelika, Alabama. Lake southeast of Auburn with bank fishing, a boat ramp, fishing pier, restrooms and concessions. Check the official lake page for current hours, permits and access.

waters.location_note: Approximate map reference published by Georgia DNR.

waters.name: Lake Jordan
waters.location_note: Approximate reservoir reference point from ADCNR’s official reservoir map. Fishery profile checked October 26, 2026.
waters.notes: Coosa River reservoir north of Montgomery, near Wetumpka. Bonner’s Point and Rotary Landing are public access areas; the Mitchell Dam tailwater is another established fishing area. Check operator information before visiting tailwaters.

waters.name: Lake Mitchell
waters.location_note: Approximate reservoir reference point from ADCNR’s official reservoir map. Fishery profile checked October 26, 2026.
waters.notes: Coosa River reservoir east of Clanton, between Lay and Jordan. Higgins Ferry is a public access area. Creeks and shoreline cover offer largemouth habitat; points, ledges and rocky structure are useful places to explore for Alabama bass.

waters.name: Lay Lake
waters.location_note: Approximate reservoir reference point from ADCNR’s official reservoir map. Fishery profile checked October 26, 2026.
waters.notes: Coosa River reservoir south of Columbiana. Creeks and shallow sloughs offer largemouth, crappie and bream habitat; riverine sections and the Logan Martin tailwater provide other fishing opportunities. Generation affects tailwater current.

waters.name: Logan Martin Lake
waters.location_note: Approximate reservoir reference point from ADCNR’s official reservoir map. Fishery profile checked October 26, 2026.
waters.notes: Coosa River reservoir between Neely Henry and Logan Martin dams, bordering St. Clair and Talladega counties. Bass and crappie are established fisheries. Headwater current and creek mouths are useful starting points for planning a visit.

links.label: ADCNR — Logan Martin Lake fishery profile

waters.name: Neely Henry Lake
waters.location_note: Approximate reservoir reference point from ADCNR’s official reservoir map. Fishery profile checked October 26, 2026.
waters.notes: Coosa River reservoir near Gadsden and Ohatchee. Much of the lake follows the river channel, opening into broader water toward the dam. Bass and crappie are established fisheries; generation influences headwater fishing.

links.label: ADCNR — Neely Henry Lake fishery profile

waters.name: Weiss Lake
waters.location_note: Approximate reservoir reference point from ADCNR’s official reservoir map. Fishery profile checked October 26, 2026.
waters.notes: Large Alabama Power reservoir on the Alabama–Georgia border near Centre. Known for crappie fishing, with largemouth and striped bass also present. Explore official public access information and verify local boating conditions before launching.

waters.name: R. E. “Bob” Woodruff Lake (Jones Bluff)
waters.manager: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Mobile District
waters.location_note: Approximate reservoir reference point from ADCNR’s official reservoir map. Fishery profile checked October 26, 2026.
waters.notes: Alabama River reservoir between Montgomery and Selma, formed by Robert F. Henry Lock and Dam. Backwaters and the main river offer different fishing conditions. Flow and generation strongly influence main-channel fishing.
